bull.b: Growing subscription revenue and a rising share of production applications indicate that D-Wave is progressing beyond experimentation toward recurring, embedded customer use. This can support a more durable software-and-services revenue base and deepen customer retention as deployments scale.

The sharp increase in bookings and remaining performance obligations provides tangible visibility into future revenue and signals stronger commercial traction. Recognition over the next two years could reduce dependence on individual customer wins and support broader platform investment.

Material solver performance gains, combined with developer training, can lower adoption barriers for complex optimization workloads. Expanding practical usability through Leap may strengthen D-Wave’s platform position and increase the pool of enterprise applications over time.

bear.b: Large and worsening operating losses show that revenue growth has not yet produced a viable earnings model. The heavy cost structure may require continued investment before scale benefits appear, increasing execution pressure and limiting financial resilience over the next several quarters.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the company is not currently funding operations internally. Continued cash consumption can increase reliance on external financing, constrain strategic flexibility, and make successful commercialization execution increasingly important.

Revenue remains highly sensitive to the timing of large system sales, creating uneven results and making near-term performance dependent on planned installations. This volatility complicates forecasting and can obscure whether recurring platform adoption is scaling fast enough to offset delivery gaps.
